newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX crude firms but indecisive after stocks data.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX crude firms but indecisive after stocks data.

text.p: NYMEX crude oil futures were firmer in early trade Wednesday and products also advanced as the market took a moderate amount of cheer from weekly inventory data showing a sharp drop in crude stocks.

At 1124 EDT, July crude was up 25 cents at $21.84 a barrel. July heating oil was a bit firmer, up 0.26 cent at 57.90 cents a gallon. June unleaded gasoline was 0.76 cent higher, trading at 66.15 cents a gallon.

Traders said most attention was focused on crude, which stemmed a two-day declining trend with moderate bullishness given by this week's American Petroleum Institute (API) and Department of Energy (DOE) inventory reports showing crude stocks fell last week by more than 5.9 million barrels and 5.4 millin barrels, respectively.

But API the data basically reversed a more than six million-barrel rise in crude stocks the previous week and the net movement since the start of May was about a 600,000 barrel rise in stocks (key API/S and hit F9 for further analysis).
Traders said the market was likely to drift quietly for a time while players await clearer direction.
"I think we're all still sorting out the recent rally and how much was actually due the June expiration," one commission house trader said.
The complex staged a rally last week that suprised many who thought last week's data showing a net build of crude stocks would have pressured value. The June contract expired after Tuesday's session.
"It's very quiet down here. Nothing's going on. Very little feature," one floor broker said.

"The market's a little indecisive here. The data gave a little bit of support to the market. The DOE (Department of Energy) numbers were a little more friendly to the products side than the API's (American Petroleum Institute)," he said.
